materials: unit-specific source, model, manipulatives, safe materials, or approved digital tool

Household-accessible route: pencil or pen and scrap paper are enough. For sound or performance work, tap, clap, use spoken syllables, move a finger, or notate silently. Specialized art materials, instruments, paid software, cameras, microphones, and recording devices are optional and never affect credit.
task_brief: Composition work on composition. Composition: arrange and revise visual relationships through composition, then use observable evidence to explain or revise a learner-owned decision. Complete the independent work yourself and explain the reason for each main choice.
primary_task: Target for this apply session: Apply composition independently in a new representation, text, situation, or design constraint. Use subject-appropriate evidence or representation to communicate understanding of composition. Check, revise, or improve work about composition using stated success criteria. Closing evidence check: In one concise response, show or explain the most important idea about composition; then identify one check that would catch an error or weak claim. What composition means here: Visual hierarchy is the order in which a composition invites attention. 1. Independent creation: Create a fresh, bounded work involving composition. State an intent, choose at least two relevant relationships, preserve one intermediate state, check the result, and make or deliberately decline one revision with a reason. 2. Critique: Describe before judging. Locate evidence, compare it with the maker’s stated intent, ask one genuine question, and offer options; the maker keeps final authority. A private self-critique receives full credit. 3. Reflection: Compare an earlier and later state. Name the choice that changed, cite what became visible, audible, notated, or workable, and state the next revision or reason to keep the result. Your choices remain yours: Different subject or abstraction, format and medium, focal point, hierarchy variables, final visual path and revision choices are valid when the learner meets objective constraints and supports the result with evidence. Keep today's work tied to your unit. Today is about composition. It is part of "Visual Elements and Observation". Later days in this unit cover other things, like line shape color texture value and space. Before you stop, do this check: In one concise response, show or explain the most important idea about composition; then identify one check that would catch an error or weak claim. In grade 5, finish on your own. Write a reason for each main choice. If there were two ways to do it, say which one you picked and why.

presentation_and_privacy.presentation_options: You choose the audience. Keeping the work entirely to yourself, showing it to one parent or trusted adult, or submitting it as a file with no one watching are all full-credit options. No public performance, exhibition, class presentation, live audience, photograph, camera, or voice recording is required at any point in this task, and choosing the most private option never lowers the score.
presentation_and_privacy.text_or_no_audio_alternative: A written alternative is always available for spoken reflection, explanation, or critique and scores the same. Tap, point through, gesture, or use the supplied notation or event map without recording. A written or notated response can show structure and reasoning; it does not claim hearing or performed control that was not actually demonstrated. No instrument, microphone, camera, or public performance is required.

copyright_and_authorship: The graded submission must be your own authorship. A parent, tutor, or AI tool may explain an idea, demonstrate a technique, or give feedback on a draft, but must not produce, write, debug, or make any part of the work that is scored. Any material you did not create yourself must be in the public domain, openly licensed, or used as a short cited excerpt for study — reproduce no more than the point requires, credit the maker and the source, and never copy full lyrics, a complete score, or a whole image and present it as your own.
accessibility_options: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, manipulatives-based, or demonstrated responses when the standard permits.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode.
task_accessibility_provisions: This task uses things you look at (composition). You may use raised or textured materials, very large print, strong colours, or a spoken description instead.
This work takes more than one sitting. Ask for a simple checklist with dates so you know what to do next. Keeping track is not part of your grade.
You can take a break, stretch, or come back to this later. That does not lower your score.
safety_and_privacy_rules: Allow a pause, break, or alternate response mode without treating it as failure.
Protect hearing, ventilation, tool safety, copyright, cultural context, and respectful representation.
Provide a non-performance or low-audience option when needed without lowering the academic target.

media.suggestion: Optional diagram, map, worked example, source image, demonstration, or short clip supporting composition.
media.fallback: Provide the same information as readable steps, alt text, transcript, tactile/concrete model, or teacher demonstration.

remediation: Route 1: Reduce composition to three locatable events, areas, steps, or decisions. Label the intended effect beside each and underline the one placement relationship that should carry it. Use a separate small study, four-event loop, thumbnail, evidence table, or paper plan. The adult may model the noticing process on different material but may not change the learner’s work. Check yourself: Point to or name the exact placement evidence before deciding whether it serves the intent. New attempt: Put the support away and make a new arrangement, passage, response, or plan; record what the new evidence shows. Route 2: Return to the last understandable state. Hold every relationship steady except one chosen feature from placement, scale, value, edge, isolation, repetition, and direction; predict what that single change should do. Test the feature on scrap paper, a silent count, a two-event rehearsal loop, movable shapes, or a short evidence sentence before changing the scored work. Check yourself: Name what stayed the same, what changed, and the first observable result—without using “better” as the evidence. New attempt: Create a different small case using the same one-variable method, then transfer the finding to the original task only if it serves the learner’s intent.
extension: Apply composition under a new constraint, compare two approaches or perspectives, or teach the idea with an original example without completing another learner’s graded work. Treat this as optional depth on composition rather than extra volume: one harder case done well beats three more of the same. Extension work stays private by default and uses only original, public-domain, or properly cited material. Extension work is never required to reach mastery and must not be assigned as a penalty.

concept_instruction.title: What composition means here
concept_instruction.body: Visual hierarchy is the order in which a composition invites attention.

concept_instruction.title: How the relationship changes the result
concept_instruction.body: A focal area becomes strong through a noticeable relationship with nearby areas; quiet space and repeated directions can lead attention to later stops.

concept_instruction.title: Choice and tradeoff
concept_instruction.body: A steep hierarchy reads quickly but can silence later areas. A shallow hierarchy can feel open but may make a precise route harder to read. Worked example: A small dark isolated form can lead a large pale form because the local value jump and open space are stronger than size alone. Non-example: Making every edge, colour, and value equally strong creates competition rather than a controllable path.

technique_sequence.action: State the intended effect or question before making or judging.
technique_sequence.notice: The statement creates a criterion that can be checked.
technique_sequence.why: Arts evidence is interpreted in relation to purpose, not personal taste.

technique_sequence.action: Identify or set up the relevant placement, scale, value, edge, isolation, repetition, and direction.
technique_sequence.notice: Locate the first relationship that can be observed in composition.
technique_sequence.why: A focal area becomes strong through a noticeable relationship with nearby areas; quiet space and repeated directions can lead attention to later stops.

technique_sequence.action: Complete one small controlled study or rehearsal loop.
technique_sequence.notice: Keep most relationships stable so one decision remains readable.
technique_sequence.why: A bounded test makes cause and effect easier to notice.

technique_sequence.action: Transfer the idea to a fresh work, excerpt, source detail, or project decision.
technique_sequence.notice: Close the model or cue before the independent decision.

technique_sequence.action: Check against criteria and choose a revision or a reasoned decision to keep the result.
technique_sequence.notice: Cite a location, moment, event, or process fact before judging.
technique_sequence.why: Evidence protects creative variation and learner authority.

common_technique_errors.observable_mismatch: The stated intent for composition is present, but the record does not yet locate placement, scale, value, edge, isolation, repetition, and direction that supports it.
common_technique_errors.not_an_error_when: The learner supports a different, ambiguous, subtle, or intentionally open effect with observable evidence.

common_technique_errors.observable_mismatch: Several relationships changed at once, so the learner cannot yet tell which choice caused the observed effect.
common_technique_errors.not_an_error_when: The task is an intentionally exploratory diagnostic and no causal claim is being scored.
